source_inputs.role: process memory/status counters with documented RSS caveat
container stats convenience surface, not independent kernel authority

findings.claim: cgroup v2 cpu.stat accounts CPU for processes in the cgroup; memory.current/memory.peak and io.stat are cgroup-level kernel interfaces.
/proc/<pid>/stat exposes utime, stime and starttime; starttime can bind samples to one PID lifetime.
/proc/<pid>/status exposes VmRSS/VmHWM but kernel documentation explicitly calls these values inaccurate.
/proc/<pid>/io exposes process I/O counters; counters have documented caveats and access controls.
pidfd_open gives a stable descriptor for an existing task and can be observed for exit; it complements but does not turn procfs process metrics into container totals.
Podman inspect/stats are useful resolver/convenience surfaces but do not erase the evidence-scope distinction between one host PID and a whole container/cgroup.

counterhypothesis: If substantial work executes in child/sibling processes, init-process CPU/RSS/I/O can materially undercount the container.
conclusion: Use a tiered witness. Prefer independently bound exact container cgroup metrics. If unavailable, emit only INIT_PROCESS_ONLY procfs evidence; container total remains UNKNOWN.
